content:
Dear Corvale Mobility hiring team,

I’m applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity role. Over the past seven years, I’ve worked in QA automation, with my recent work focused on CI/CD pipelines, test infrastructure and build tooling. At Odrava Health Software, I own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams and have built short-lived environments for merge requests using Docker Compose and, later, Helm on a shared Kubernetes cluster.

I’ve improved the teams’ delivery infrastructure through practical, measurable changes: parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and separating end-to-end tests reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes, while monthly CI runner costs fell by about 30%. I also maintain a roughly 900-test pytest and Playwright suite, with the flaky-test rate reduced from 7% to below 1%, and built dashboards that help teams investigate reliability issues. These projects have involved working across QA and product teams and making infrastructure easier to use and understand; I also wrote the internal CI guide used in onboarding.

Alongside my professional work, I’ve built a personal three-node k3s cluster with GitOps using Argo CD, monitoring with Prometheus, Grafana and Loki, and Terraform-provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS. My Terraform and cloud experience is developing: I’ve used Terraform in that personal project and explored AWS EC2 and S3 through free-tier learning. I’m currently preparing for the CKA exam; I have not yet earned the certification.

Corvale’s plan to connect a new train fleet to its cloud platform is an appealing infrastructure challenge, and your emphasis on teams owning systems end to end fits the way I like to work: improving the tools and environments that help teams build, test and operate their services. I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience in CI/CD and test infrastructure could contribute to the Fleet Connectivity team.

Kind regards,
Marta Kowal-Brandt

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, professional, well structured, and appropriately concise. It uses credible, quantified achievements rather than generic claims: pipeline duration improved from 38 to 14 minutes, CI runner costs fell by about 30%, and flaky tests decreased from 7% to below 1%. It also transparently describes the limits of the candidate’s Terraform, AWS, and CKA experience, which strengthens credibility. The main content weakness is that it presents the candidate primarily as a QA automation engineer and does not make the strongest supported connections to infrastructure engineering, technical ownership, TLS, Linux, and stakeholder communication.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is ATS-friendly in plain text: it has a conventional greeting, readable paragraphs, no tables or graphics, and includes relevant terms such as CI/CD, GitLab CI, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes, GitOps, Argo CD, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Terraform, AWS EC2, and S3. AI screening may still rank it as a developing or adjacent match because key job terms such as infrastructure engineering, cloud environment operation, systems architecture, system design, networking, TLS, security awareness, and stakeholder alignment are either absent or only indirectly represented. The cover letter cannot truthfully claim strong Terraform/Terragrunt, mTLS, or production cloud experience, so those omissions are appropriate gaps rather than ATS defects.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest alignment is with hands-on test infrastructure, CI/CD ownership, Kubernetes-based environments, observability, analytical improvement, and clear technical documentation. The emphasis on owning systems, improving developer workflows, and collaborating across QA and product teams also fits Corvale’s engineering-led and end-to-end ownership culture. However, the candidate’s material indicates gaps against several core requirements: strong Terraform and Terragrunt, mTLS and broader networking, production cloud environment operation, system architecture at the required level, and IoT or remote-device integration. The letter appropriately does not overstate these areas. It could better highlight supported evidence around TLS configuration, Linux, technical ownership, and bringing users or teams along with infrastructure changes.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES: None identified. The cover letter contains no clear unsupported skills, certifications, tools, or experiences when cross-referenced with the Original Candidate Information.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the second paragraph, after the sentence ending “reliability issues,” add the supported technical ownership evidence: “I also own the CI workflow used by approximately 25 developers across three teams, and I wrote the internal CI guide used in onboarding.” This makes leadership, communication, and stakeholder enablement more explicit without claiming formal people or architecture leadership.
2. In the third paragraph, after the sentence describing the k3s cluster, add the supported security and networking detail: “The homelab also includes Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS, alongside Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for observability.” This introduces the job’s TLS, ingress, and observability terminology truthfully. Do not describe this as mutual TLS or production-grade security.
3. In the final paragraph, replace “my experience in CI/CD and test infrastructure” with “my experience in CI/CD, Kubernetes-based test infrastructure, observability, and developer-facing tooling.” This better reflects the strongest overlap with the role while remaining accurate.
4. In the third paragraph, change “Terraform and cloud experience is developing” to “My Terraform and cloud experience is currently centred on a personal Hetzner project and AWS EC2 and S3 learning.” This is more concrete and ATS-readable while preserving the important limitation that the experience is not professional production-cloud experience.
5. If space permits, add “Linux” to the sentence describing the personal infrastructure project, using wording such as “a three-node Linux k3s cluster.” This is supported by the associated CV and candidate information and directly addresses a listed nice-to-have.

Marta Kowal-Brandt

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is professional, credible and supported by the candidate information. It uses strong quantified evidence, including the reduction in pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes, the 30% runner-cost reduction, the approximately 900-test suite and the reduction in flaky tests from 7% to below 1%. It also establishes relevant experience with CI/CD, Kubernetes-based test environments, observability and developer-facing tooling. However, the letter contains noticeable repetition: the internal CI guide is mentioned twice in the same paragraph, and Prometheus, Grafana and Loki are repeated in the following paragraph. The opening also presents a QA-to-cloud transition without explicitly framing how the candidate's infrastructure responsibilities transfer to this role. The CKA and cloud-experience disclosure is truthful but occupies space that could be used to foreground system design, TLS, technical leadership and stakeholder collaboration.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is plain-text friendly, uses standard paragraphs, contains no problematic tables or graphics, and includes useful keywords such as CI/CD, GitLab CI, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS, observability, PostgreSQL, Python and Bash. ATS and AI screening probability is moderate rather than high because several central job terms are absent or weakly represented in the letter: systems architecture, system design, networking, SSL/TLS, certificate management, security awareness, stakeholder alignment and technical proposals. Terraform is mentioned only in the context of a personal project, and Terragrunt is correctly not claimed because it is not in the candidate information. The duplicated sentences may also make the letter appear less carefully edited.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest alignment is with hands-on infrastructure work around CI/CD, ephemeral environments, Kubernetes, observability, reliability improvement, Linux-based systems and clear technical documentation. The candidate also demonstrates ownership across three teams and communication through onboarding documentation and cross-team use of dashboards. The main substantive gaps are strong Terraform and Terragrunt experience, production cloud infrastructure operation, mTLS, broader networking, direct IoT or remote-device integration, and backend/full-stack development. AWS experience is limited to free-tier learning with EC2 and S3, while Terraform is limited to a personal Hetzner project. The letter should present the strongest transferable evidence without implying production-cloud, mTLS, fleet-connectivity or backend experience that the candidate does not have. The culture connection to end-to-end ownership is relevant and credible, but it could be tied more directly to the candidate's demonstrated ownership of CI pipelines and test infrastructure.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL: In the third paragraph, remove the duplicated sentence "I also wrote the internal CI guide used in onboarding." Keep it once only, preferably after the sentence about owning the CI workflow for approximately 25 developers.

CRITICAL: In the fourth paragraph, remove the repeated observability wording. Replace "The homelab also includes Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS, alongside Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for observability" with "The homelab also includes Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS." Prometheus, Grafana and Loki have already been mentioned in the preceding sentence.

In the second paragraph, make the technical leadership and stakeholder impact more explicit using only existing evidence. Replace "I also own the CI workflow used by approximately 25 developers across three teams, and I wrote the internal CI guide used in onboarding. These projects have involved working across QA and product teams and making infrastructure easier to use and understand" with "I own the CI workflow used by approximately 25 developers across three teams and wrote the internal CI guide used in onboarding. By making the pipeline and test environments easier to use, I helped QA and product teams review changes and investigate reliability issues more effectively." 

In the first or second paragraph, explicitly describe the system-design scope already supported by the candidate's experience. For example, add after the ephemeral-environment sentence: "This involved designing the flow from merge-request creation through application, PostgreSQL and seeded-data deployment, automated end-to-end testing and environment removal after merge or 48 hours of inactivity." This improves alignment with system design without claiming broader production architecture experience.

In the fourth paragraph, make the truthful TLS and infrastructure evidence more relevant to the security and networking aspects of the role. Replace the current homelab description with: "Alongside my professional work, I built a personal three-node Linux k3s cluster with GitOps using Argo CD, Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS, with Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring. I also provisioned a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform." Do not add mTLS, network-design or production-security claims, because they are not supported by the candidate information.

In the final paragraph, connect the candidate's actual ownership experience more directly to Corvale's stated end-to-end ownership culture. Replace "your emphasis on teams owning systems end to end fits the way I like to work" with "your emphasis on teams owning systems end to end aligns with my experience owning CI pipelines and test infrastructure used by three product teams, and with my interest in making systems easier to build, test and operate."
critique.critical_issues: No factual hallucinations were detected: the technical tools, metrics, personal-project scope, AWS learning status and CKA status are consistent with the original candidate information. The critical document defects are duplicated content about the internal CI guide and repeated observability tools; both should be removed to improve precision and professionalism.

content:
Dear Corvale Mobility hiring team,

I’m applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity role. Over the past seven years, I’ve worked in QA automation, with my recent work focused on CI/CD pipelines, test infrastructure and build tooling. At Odrava Health Software, I own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams and have built short-lived environments for merge requests using Docker Compose and, later, Helm on a shared Kubernetes cluster. This involved designing the flow from merge-request creation through application, PostgreSQL and seeded-data deployment, automated end-to-end testing and environment removal after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.

I’ve improved the teams’ delivery infrastructure through practical, measurable changes: parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and separating end-to-end tests reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes, while monthly CI runner costs fell by about 30%. I also maintain a roughly 900-test pytest and Playwright suite, with the flaky-test rate reduced from 7% to below 1%, and built dashboards that help teams investigate reliability issues. I own the CI workflow used by approximately 25 developers across three teams and wrote the internal CI guide used in onboarding. By making the pipeline and test environments easier to use, I helped QA and product teams review changes and investigate reliability issues more effectively.

Alongside my professional work, I built a personal three-node Linux k3s cluster with GitOps using Argo CD, Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS, with Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring. I also provisioned a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform. My Terraform and cloud experience is currently centred on a personal Hetzner project and AWS EC2 and S3 learning. I’m currently preparing for the CKA exam; I have not yet earned the certification.

Corvale’s plan to connect a new train fleet to its cloud platform is an appealing infrastructure challenge, and your emphasis on teams owning systems end to end aligns with my experience owning CI pipelines and test infrastructure used by three product teams, and with my interest in making systems easier to build, test and operate. I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience in CI/CD, Kubernetes-based test infrastructure, observability, and developer-facing tooling could contribute to the Fleet Connectivity team.

Kind regards,
Marta Kowal-Brandt

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, professional, well tailored to the Fleet Connectivity role, and supported by concrete evidence. It uses strong measurable outcomes: pipeline time reduced from 38 to 14 minutes, CI runner costs reduced by approximately 30%, and flaky tests reduced from 7% to below 1%. It also accurately presents the candidate's transition from QA automation into CI/CD and platform infrastructure without overstating certification, cloud, or Kubernetes experience. The main content limitation is that it gives little direct evidence related to systems architecture, networking, security practice, stakeholder leadership, or technical proposals; however, several of these are genuine experience gaps rather than writing defects.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly in plain text, uses standard paragraphs, and includes relevant terms such as CI/CD, GitLab CI, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS EC2, AWS S3, Argo CD, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, TLS, PostgreSQL, pytest, and Playwright. The structure is easy to parse. Adding a simple header with the candidate's name, contact details, date, company name, and role title would improve document completeness and keyword context. The letter does not use unsupported keywords such as Terragrunt, mTLS, or production cloud operations, which is appropriate and strengthens its credibility. AI screening probability is good for CI/CD, test infrastructure, Kubernetes-based environments, observability, and developer tooling, but weaker for strong Terraform/Terragrunt, cloud infrastructure operation, networking, and security.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows a credible match for hands-on infrastructure-adjacent engineering, CI/CD ownership, Kubernetes-based test environments, observability, analytical problem-solving, and clear technical communication. The candidate also shows relevant Linux, TLS/certificate-management, AWS learning, and Terraform experience through personal projects. The principal alignment gaps are that Terraform is limited to a personal Hetzner project, Terragrunt is not present, mTLS is not demonstrated, broader cloud environment operation is limited, and there is no IoT, automotive, remote-device, backend, or virtual-machine experience in the candidate material. The letter appropriately discloses the limited AWS and Terraform scope and the fact that the CKA is not yet earned. Evidence for leading technical topics is moderate: pipeline ownership, cross-team improvements, onboarding documentation, and mentoring are relevant, but the material does not show leading architecture proposals or coordinating with external manufacturers.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENT 1 — At the top of the cover letter, add a compact ATS-friendly header containing “Marta Kowal-Brandt,” email, phone, GitLab URL, the date, “Corvale Mobility,” and “Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity.” Keep the existing salutation below this header.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT 2 — In the paragraph beginning “Alongside my professional work,” make the scope of the Kubernetes and Terraform experience even more precise by changing the first sentence to: “Alongside my professional work, I built a three-node Linux k3s cluster with GitOps using Argo CD, Traefik ingress, cert-manager for TLS, and Prometheus, Grafana, and Loki for monitoring; professionally, my Kubernetes work is at namespace level on a shared cluster.” This makes the relevant experience clearer while preventing the reader from interpreting it as cluster administration.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT 3 — In the second paragraph, replace “I own the CI workflow used by approximately 25 developers across three teams” with “I own GitLab CI pipelines used by approximately 25 developers across three product teams.” This uses the job-relevant technology name already supported by the candidate's experience and is more precise for ATS screening.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT 4 — In the final paragraph, reduce repetition of “owning” and make the demonstrated stakeholder impact more explicit. Replace the final sentence with: “I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience improving CI/CD, Kubernetes-based test infrastructure, observability, and developer-facing tooling could support the Fleet Connectivity team.”
